text: Mortar Source Guns & Gears (Remastered) pg. 176 Price 720 gp Ammunition mortar round (5 gp, 1 Bulk) --- Usage mounted (black powder) Space 8 feet long, 4 feet wide, 5 feet high Crew 3-4 Proficiency martial --- AC 20 Fort +15 Ref +8 Hardness 12 HP 40 Immunities object immunities --- Speed 20 feet (pulled or pushed) --- A mortar fires its shells at a high angle, allowing it to bypass obstacles and strike from above. A crew typically sets up such a weapon behind a wall or in another hard-to-access area to protect themselves while retaining full functionality. Due to the steep angle of its arc, such mortars are especially useful when opposing barricaded targets. Aim Two Actions 40 feet, minimum distance 50 feet Load Two Actions (manipulate) 3 times Launch Two Actions (manipulate, range increment 100 feet) 5d10 slashing, 20-foot burst, DC 21. Because a mortar launches its round at a high angle, the mortar round descends on the center of the burst from above, not in a straight line from the mortar. This affects whether creatures have cover from the mortar launch.
markdown:
**Source** [Guns & Gears (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=98) pg. 176 **Price** 720 gp **Ammunition** mortar round (5 gp, 1 Bulk) --- **Usage** mounted (black powder) **Space** 8 feet long, 4 feet wide, 5 feet high **Crew** 3-4 **Proficiency** martial --- **AC** 20 **Fort** +15 **Ref** +8 **Hardness** 12 **HP** 40 **Immunities** object immunities --- **Speed** 20 feet (pulled or pushed) --- A mortar fires its shells at a high angle, allowing it to bypass obstacles and strike from above. A crew typically sets up such a weapon behind a wall or in another hard-to-access area to protect themselves while retaining full functionality. Due to the steep angle of its arc, such mortars are especially useful when opposing barricaded targets.
**Aim** 40 feet, minimum distance 50 feet
**Load** ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104)) 3 times
**Launch** ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104), [range increment 100 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=248)) 5d10 slashing, 20-foot burst, DC 21. Because a mortar launches its round at a high angle, the mortar round descends on the center of the burst from above, not in a straight line from the mortar. This affects whether creatures have cover from the mortar launch.
